target: A storage team ran 30 independent disaster-recovery drills representative of the planned deployment and observed zero irreversible-loss events. The launch rule requires 95% confidence that the true irreversible-loss probability per drill is below 5%. The team must decide whether zero observed losses in these 30 drills is enough to certify the launch.
surface: A previous storage launch treated a clean recovery dashboard as sufficient: after 30 disaster-recovery drills with zero irreversible-loss events, it certified the launch because the observed loss rate was 0%.
structural: In a clinical safety study with n independent exposures and zero observed adverse events, reviewers used the 95% 'rule of three': the upper confidence bound on the event probability is approximately 3/n. They compared that upper bound, rather than the observed zero rate, with the safety ceiling before declaring the sample adequate.
rubric: Explicitly selects the zero-event 95% rule-of-three upper confidence bound.
Reports an upper bound of about 0.10 (10%).
Concludes 30 clean drills do not establish a below-5% loss probability and does not certify launch.
States the independence/representativeness assumption or identifies that roughly 60 clean trials would only bring the approximation to 5%.
